Run the actual Park engine

The important difference

An example is part
of the running system.

=

Known answers come first.

A call matching an authored example returns that answer. It works even before there is code.

+

Code fills the gaps.

A developer writes the general rule. Explicit checks run the implementation against its examples and report disagreements.

?

Missing facts become questions.

If neither an example nor an implementation answers a call, Park records the missing answer. Code errors are reported as errors.

Two examples make an implemented function “ready” under the current policy. That count alone does not prove correctness; checks are a separate step.

What to evaluate in a pilot

Can your rule owner answer a missing case? Can a developer check the rule? Can a reviewer understand the change before activation?

These are candidate use cases, not customer deployments. Park evaluates pure rules; applications remain responsible for actions such as payments, emails, and database updates.

For developers & SaaS builders

A small runtime.
A different contract.

Go + Starlark, compiled to WebAssembly for the browser. Deterministic functions, explicit examples, and traceable answers.

Zones.zone("DE")"international"Answered by the saved example

Examples answer.
Checks verify.

Runtime lookup gives the example precedence. park test bypasses the target function’s own examples and cache to test its implementation.

Keep the rule boundary small.

No network, files, clock, or randomness inside rules. Supply inputs from your application; inspect results and provenance.

Read the technical rationale

The local backend is already here

A new answer shouldn’t
be an accidental release.

Draft

Save the change.

Edit an isolated copy. Keep source history and reject stale writes.

Review

See the impact.

Check implementations and compare named scenarios against pinned source and release versions.

Activate

Make it live.

Approve a whole-project release. Evaluate that release, or roll back to an earlier one.

Working locally, with SQLite persistence.

Reviews use local actor labels. Hosted accounts, tenant permissions, authenticated reviewer roles, and operations are still planned. Comparisons cover the selected scenarios.
